paragraphs: Learning new visual categories can make a model forget categories it learned earlier. Federated learning makes this harder because users hold separate datasets that can change independently. Approaches developed for centralized training do not transfer directly when users face privacy concerns and limits on storage or computation.

The paper introduces a federated class incremental learning framework that generates synthetic examples representing past data distributions. Those examples can accompany current training data, giving the model a way to revisit earlier learning. After each task, a generative model is trained on the server through a data-free procedure that does not request client data. Users also do not need to retain old datasets or models.

These choices support users joining or leaving training without maintaining their own historical training resources. The researchers additionally introduce SuperImageNet, a regrouping of ImageNet designed for federated continual learning. Experiments across multiple datasets report significant improvements over existing baselines, supporting synthetic replay as a practical way to reduce forgetting in this distributed setting.
neurips-2023-a-data-free-approach-to-mit.tldr: Server-trained synthetic replay reduces forgetting in federated vision learning without requiring clients to retain old data or models.

paragraphs: High-dimensional mediation analysis involves testing many candidate mediators and deciding which ones are relevant. With many simultaneous tests, some selections can be false discoveries. The paper treats this as two connected decisions: how to rank the hypotheses and where to place the cutoff for selecting mediators.

AMDP combines an optimal hypothesis ranking rule with a selection threshold learned from the data. Its construction uses information about the proportions of different composite null hypotheses and the distribution of p-values across tests. Sharing this information across the testing problem addresses shortcomings of approaches that leave p-values uncalibrated or ignore relationships in the available testing information.

The procedure is designed to control the false discovery rate asymptotically, so its guarantee concerns the limiting statistical regime rather than an unconditional guarantee for every finite dataset. The central contribution is that a large collection of tests can supply useful information for ranking and selection. Numerical studies on synthetic and real datasets illustrate AMDP's performance relative to existing approaches.
neurips-2023-amdp-an-adaptive-detection-.tldr: AMDP uses information across mediation tests to rank candidates optimally and select them while asymptotically controlling false discoveries.

paragraphs: Training an image reconstruction model usually benefits from paired noisy measurements and clean images, but clean references can be difficult to collect. Self-supervised methods remove that requirement by learning from noisy measurements alone. This paper asks how much additional training data is needed to make up for the missing clean targets.

The analysis covers methods, including noise2noise, that can produce unbiased estimates of the supervised loss gradient. In this setting, the estimated training direction is correct on average. The authors show analytically that self-supervised training can make the same model as good as supervised training, although reaching that performance requires more examples.

Experiments on image denoising and accelerated MRI examine this additional sample requirement. They find that the performance gap shrinks away as the number of training examples grows, with the rate depending on the reconstruction problem. The result frames the tradeoff as a data requirement: for the analyzed class of methods, avoiding clean references need not impose a lasting performance disadvantage.
neurips-2023-analyzing-the-sample-comple.tldr: For the analyzed self-supervised reconstruction methods, matching supervised performance requires more examples, with the gap closing at a problem-dependent rate.

paragraphs: Healthcare question answering has largely centered on medical images, clinical notes, and structured health records. ECG-QA extends this research direction to electrocardiograms, creating a dataset specifically for questions about ECG interpretation. The contribution is a resource for connecting natural-language questions with this type of clinical signal.

The dataset is organized around 70 question templates spanning clinically relevant ECG topics. An ECG expert validated each template for clinical utility. Its questions include interpretation of individual recordings as well as comparisons between two ECGs, broadening the task beyond answering questions about one recording in isolation.

The authors also conduct experiments intended to inform future research on ECG question answering. Together, the templates, expert validation, and comparative questions define a setting in which researchers can develop systems that respond to varied ECG interpretation requests. The stated goal is to support future tools that assist clinicians; the abstract presents a dataset and research experiments, rather than a demonstrated clinical deployment.
neurips-2023-ecg-qa-a-comprehensive-ques.tldr: ECG-QA provides expert-validated question templates and ECG interpretation questions, including comparisons between recordings, to support healthcare question-answering research.

paragraphs: Experimental design decides which measurements to collect to learn efficiently. Many linear formulations assume every measurement has the same noise level, although reliability can vary across measurement choices. This paper studies a finite collection of measurement vectors whose responses depend linearly on an unknown parameter.

The analysis assumes independent, mean-zero sub-Gaussian noise, with a variance parameter that is a quadratic function of the measurement vector through an unknown matrix. The authors develop a measurement design that uniformly bounds estimation error for these variance parameters. Learning how reliability varies across measurements provides information that a constant-noise design would overlook.

They apply the approach to identifying the best option and identifying options relative to a level threshold, under heteroskedastic noise. For these settings, they establish instance-dependent lower bounds and construct near-optimal algorithms. Empirical results show large reductions in sample requirements from accounting for varying noise. The contribution links estimating measurement reliability to making subsequent measurement choices more efficiently.
neurips-2023-experimental-designs-for-he.tldr: Estimating how noise varies across measurements enables near-optimal experimental designs and empirically reduces the samples needed for identification tasks.

paragraphs: Contrastive analysis looks for variation enriched in a target dataset relative to a background dataset representing variation irrelevant to the task. In a biomedical example, researchers might seek a small set of genes that captures variation specific to patients with a disease, using healthy controls as the background.

The paper introduces contrastive feature selection, or CFS, to choose features for this particular objective. Its motivation comes from an information-theoretic analysis of representation learning in the contrastive setting. The distinction matters because features useful for general prediction or for describing all variation need not capture the variation uniquely enriched in the target population.

The authors evaluate CFS on one semi-synthetic dataset and four real-world biomedical datasets. It consistently outperforms the compared state-of-the-art supervised and fully unsupervised feature selection methods, which were not designed for contrastive analysis. These findings support matching feature selection to the target-versus-background question when the goal is a compact description of target-specific variation.
neurips-2023-feature-selection-in-the-co.tldr: CFS selects features for target-specific variation and outperforms compared general-purpose feature selection methods on the evaluated datasets.

paragraphs: Pool-based active learning chooses which examples from an available collection should receive labels. This paper studies that choice for multiclass classification with multinomial logistic regression. Its goal is to connect the selection criterion directly to the classifier's excess risk, the extra risk relative to the reference optimum.

Through finite-sample analysis, the authors show that the Fisher Information Ratio provides both lower and upper bounds on excess risk. This makes the ratio a theoretically motivated quantity to optimize when selecting examples. Their algorithm, FIRAL, uses regret minimization to reduce this ratio, translating the statistical analysis into an active learning procedure.

Synthetic-data experiments examine the derived risk bounds. The authors also compare FIRAL against five other methods on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and 50-class ImageNet. FIRAL consistently achieves the smallest classification error in those multiclass logistic regression experiments. The evidence therefore combines a bounded-risk selection principle with empirical support in the specific model setting the paper analyzes.
neurips-2023-firal-an-active-learning-al.tldr: FIRAL selects examples by minimizing a Fisher-information criterion that bounds excess risk, achieving the lowest classification error in its reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Two related sources of data can contain both shared information and information specific to each source. This paper develops a way to quantify that distinction and separate the corresponding representations. The objective is to identify what the sources have in common while retaining a description of what makes each one different.

The authors define common information through an optimization problem over a family of functions. Their definition includes Gacs-Korner common information as a special case and can be approximated using samples from the data distribution. They then modify a conventional variational autoencoder to partition and quantify shared and unique information within a learned representation.

Experiments show semantically meaningful shared and source-specific factors in high-dimensional data, including images and videos. On datasets with known underlying latent factors, the method also accurately quantifies common information. These results connect the proposed information measure to a practical representation-learning procedure, with quantitative validation where the underlying factors are available for comparison.
neurips-2023-gacs-korner-common-informat.tldr: A modified variational autoencoder separates and quantifies shared and unique information using a sample-based generalization of Gacs-Korner common information.

paragraphs: Large web-scraped image collections can carry stereotypical biases, include personally identifiable information, and disproportionately represent Europe and North America. GeoDE explores a different collection approach: asking people around the world to contribute images. The resulting dataset contains 61,940 images covering 40 object classes across six world regions, without personally identifiable information.

The researchers analyze how images collected through this process differ from web-scraped images. This makes collection strategy part of the research question, alongside the dataset's role in object recognition. Geographic coverage provides a basis for examining model shortcomings that might be less apparent in data drawn from more concentrated sources.

GeoDE is used for both evaluation and training. The experiments expose weaknesses in current models and demonstrate improved performance from training with this comparatively small collection. The findings show that a geographically diverse dataset can contribute useful training information as well as a broader evaluation resource. The paper releases the dataset and accompanying code for further use.
neurips-2023-geode-a-geographically-dive.tldr: GeoDE collects geographically diverse object images from contributors worldwide, revealing model shortcomings and improving performance when used for training.

paragraphs: Backdoor attacks on federated learning introduce hidden behavior into a shared model during distributed training. A particular input pattern later activates that behavior. The paper highlights weaknesses in earlier attacks, including conspicuous triggers, demanding assumptions about attacker access, and effects that fade after the attacker stops participating.

IBA combines learning a visually subtle trigger with gradually introducing the backdoor into the global model. Its design also targets model parameters that the main learning task is less likely to change and keeps malicious updates close to the global model. These mechanisms aim to make the attack harder to notice and less vulnerable to being overwritten by subsequent training.

Evaluations on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Tiny ImageNet report high attack success, evasion of existing defenses, and greater persistence than the compared attacks. These findings identify a security concern involving both detectability and durability. Despite the framework's name, the stated evidence supports a more durable backdoor effect, rather than a universal guarantee that the attack is irreversible.
neurips-2023-iba-towards-irreversible-ba.tldr: IBA produces stealthier, longer-lasting federated-learning backdoors and bypasses existing defenses in the reported benchmark evaluations.

paragraphs: Constrained reinforcement learning seeks a good policy while satisfying specified requirements. Lagrangian policy search can produce oscillating policies, creating constraint violations and sensitivity to hyperparameters. This paper studies infinite-horizon discounted constrained Markov decision processes and asks whether the policy currently produced by an algorithm converges to an optimal constrained policy.

The authors express the problem as a saddle-point interaction between policy and dual variables, then introduce two algorithms that update both on a single timescale. RPG-PD combines an entropy-regularized policy update with a quadratically regularized dual update. Its policy-dual iterates converge sublinearly to a regularized saddle point, and its policies converge sublinearly to an optimal constrained policy.

The paper also extends RPG-PD to policy function approximation for large state or action spaces, establishing similar policy convergence. Its second method, OPG-PD, uses optimistic gradient updates and achieves linear convergence to a saddle point containing an optimal constrained policy. These non-asymptotic results address the final policy iterate directly, and computational experiments further support the methods.
neurips-2023-last-iterate-convergent-pol.tldr: Two single-timescale policy-gradient methods provide last-iterate convergence guarantees for constrained reinforcement learning, with sublinear and linear rates respectively.

paragraphs: Concept erasure removes specified information from a model's representation. It can help investigate whether a model relies on a linguistic feature or reduce its use of sensitive attributes. The challenge is to remove the target concept while preserving as much of the remaining representation as possible.

LEACE provides a closed-form transformation that provably prevents all linear classifiers from detecting the target concept. At the same time, it minimizes the change to the representation under a broad class of norms. These two properties connect a precise removal guarantee with a precise notion of preserving the original representation. The guarantee is specifically about linear detection.

The authors also introduce concept scrubbing, which applies erasure throughout every layer of a language model. They demonstrate the approach by measuring language models' reliance on part-of-speech information and reducing gender bias in BERT embeddings. The applications show how a controlled representation change can serve both as an interpretability intervention and as a tool for addressing a particular form of bias.
neurips-2023-leace-perfect-linear-concep.tldr: LEACE removes linearly detectable concept information with minimal representation change and supports concept scrubbing across language-model layers.

paragraphs: Video moment retrieval finds the segment of an untrimmed video that matches a language description. MomentDiff treats the segment's location as something to generate through progressive refinement. It begins with random temporal guesses and uses the relationship between the video and the text to move toward the relevant moment.

During training, the method corrupts a true segment span into noise and learns to reverse that process with guidance from text-video similarity. At inference, it repeatedly refines randomly initialized spans to estimate temporal boundaries. The authors argue that this random initialization can resist dataset biases about where relevant events tend to occur.

To examine those biases, the paper introduces Charades-STA-Len and Charades-STA-Mom, two evaluation datasets with shifts in temporal location distributions. MomentDiff consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on three public benchmarks and shows better generalization and robustness on these additional datasets. The results support iterative span generation as an effective retrieval approach under both standard evaluation and the tested distribution shifts.
neurips-2023-momentdiff-generative-video.tldr: MomentDiff refines random video spans through text-guided diffusion, improving retrieval and robustness to tested temporal location shifts.

paragraphs: Estimating surface normals from a 3D point cloud means recovering directions associated with the underlying surface. Existing learned methods often depend on normal labels from synthetic shapes, while real scans usually lack those labels. Making the normal directions consistently oriented also presents a challenge.

NeuralGF learns oriented normals directly from point clouds without ground-truth normal supervision. It trains a neural function to fit the cloud while producing unit-length gradients at its points. Its losses guide query points toward an approximated surface, building a global surface representation. Incorporating gradients into signed surface-deviation measurements helps produce a consistent gradient field from which normals can be estimated.

The reported estimator is robust to noise, outliers, and variations in point density. On widely used benchmarks, it produces more accurate results than the latest compared methods for both oriented and unoriented normal estimation. The approach connects surface reconstruction and normal estimation within one learned representation, reducing dependence on supervised normal labels and a separate orientation-fixing stage.
neurips-2023-neuralgf-unsupervised-point.tldr: NeuralGF learns a global surface and consistent gradient field to estimate accurate oriented point-cloud normals without normal supervision.

paragraphs: Pre-training can improve a model before it is adapted to a smaller target dataset, but the properties that make pre-training useful for robustness are less obvious. This paper examines how the pre-training distribution affects a fine-tuned model's ability to generalize under distribution shift.

The study varies the label space, label meanings, image diversity, data domains, and total amount of pre-training data. Across the investigated conditions, data quantity is the main factor associated with downstream effective robustness, while the other factors have limited significance. One example reduces ImageNet's number of pre-training classes fourfold and increases images per class fourfold, keeping the total fixed without affecting fine-tuned robustness.

The experiments use pre-training distributions from natural and synthetic sources, primarily testing robustness through the iWildCam-WILDS distribution shift. The findings suggest that total data volume deserves particular attention when interpreting robustness gains in these settings. Their scope is the studied distributions and evaluations, so the result does not establish that diversity is irrelevant to every downstream task.
neurips-2023-on-the-connection-between-p.tldr: In the studied pre-training settings, data quantity influences fine-tuned effective robustness more strongly than the examined forms of diversity.

paragraphs: Arguments about why stochastic optimization works in deep learning have sometimes focused on whether gradient noise has heavy tails. This paper investigates that question with formal statistical tests and emphasizes that the answer depends on how gradients are examined: across parameter dimensions or across training iterations.

The tests find that dimension-wise gradients usually show power-law heavy tails. In contrast, iteration-wise gradients and gradient noise introduced by minibatch training usually do not. These qualified findings distinguish properties of the gradients themselves from properties of their noise, and distinguish variation across coordinates from variation over time.

The authors also identify power-law structure in the covariance spectra of stochastic gradients and discuss theoretical implications for network training. This adds a more specific description to the broader observation that gradient variability differs across directions. Together, the results suggest that understanding stochastic gradients requires attention to their organization across dimensions and correlations, rather than assigning one heavy-tail label to every aspect of the training process.
neurips-2023-on-the-overlooked-structure.tldr: Statistical tests distinguish heavy tails across gradient dimensions from their usual absence across iterations and reveal power-law covariance structure.

paragraphs: Black-box variational inference uses stochastic optimization to fit an approximate distribution in an inference problem. Although widely used, it often operates without a proof that the optimization will converge. This paper identifies a gap between the mathematical behavior of its gradient estimators and the assumptions handled by existing convergence arguments.

Two obstacles are central: unusual bounds on gradient-estimation noise and an objective combining components that need not all be smooth. For dense Gaussian variational families, the authors observe that existing reparameterization-based gradient estimators satisfy a quadratic noise bound. They use this property as the basis for an analysis tailored to the optimization problem.

The resulting guarantees cover proximal and projected stochastic gradient descent. They establish convergence for methods similar to practical inference procedures on realistic problems within the analyzed setting. The contribution is therefore a theoretical bridge from the actual noise behavior of these estimators to justified optimization methods, with dense Gaussian families providing the specific scope of the result.
neurips-2023-provable-convergence-guaran.tldr: A quadratic gradient-noise bound enables convergence guarantees for proximal and projected stochastic optimization in dense Gaussian variational inference.

paragraphs: Monte Carlo path tracing produces realistic images, but using few samples leaves substantial noise. Real-time rendering therefore needs to make limited samples useful while removing noise effectively. This paper develops a jointly trained system that connects adaptive sampling, learned sample representation, and neural denoising.

A sampling importance network is optimized through reinforcement learning, avoiding explicit numerically approximated gradients for that component. The system preserves all sampled values instead of immediately averaging them within each pixel. A latent-space encoder processes those values and learns representations in place of handcrafted spatial and temporal heuristics. A denoiser then refines the output image.

Keeping the samples available gives the learned encoder access to information before per-pixel averaging would collapse it. Across several challenging datasets, the authors report improved visual quality and a 1.6-fold rendering speedup at equal quality compared with the previous state of the art. These results support jointly learning sampling and reconstruction as a promising approach to faster, higher-quality path-traced rendering.
neurips-2023-rl-based-stateful-neural-ad.tldr: Jointly learned sampling, sample encoding, and denoising deliver a reported 1.6-fold path-tracing speedup at equal visual quality.

paragraphs: A reinforcement learning agent can rely on relationships that hold during training but change when hidden influences change. The paper illustrates this with traffic conditions and time of day, whose association can reflect unobserved human activity. A policy that depends on that association may fail when the testing environment differs.

The authors introduce Robust State-Confounded Markov Decision Processes to model robustness against this kind of spurious correlation. The challenge is that the relevant uncertainty depends on unobserved confounders and causal structure, making it difficult to describe or identify. Simple, unstructured uncertainty sets used by other robust methods do not adequately capture this problem.

The paper provides theoretical results showing advantages over other robust reinforcement learning formulations in avoiding spurious correlations. It also develops an empirical algorithm for learning the framework's robust optimal policy. That algorithm outperforms all evaluated baselines across eight realistic driving and manipulation tasks, supporting the value of representing confounding explicitly in the robustness objective.
neurips-2023-seeing-is-not-believing-rob.tldr: A robust decision-process framework explicitly accounts for hidden state confounding and improves performance across eight tested driving and manipulation tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies how diffusion generation changes as a sample develops. It describes two phases: early dynamics near a central fixed point and later dynamics attracted toward the data manifold. A change in the central point's stability separates them, with the resulting unstable interval responsible for diversity among generated samples.

Theoretical and empirical evidence indicates that accurately simulating the early phase contributes little to final generation because early fluctuations return toward the central fixed point. This suggests an opportunity to avoid spending computation on details that the dynamics subsequently undo. The authors turn that observation into a Gaussian late initialization scheme.

The proposed initialization improves fast-sampler performance, with reported FID improvements of up to threefold, and increases sample diversity. The diversity examples include the racial composition of generated CelebA images. The work connects a dynamical explanation of generation to a practical sampling modification, while presenting higher performance and reduced bias as potential benefits of this perspective.
neurips-2023-spontaneous-symmetry-breaki.tldr: A two-phase account of diffusion dynamics motivates Gaussian late initialization, improving fast-sampler FID and sample diversity in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Small adversarial image changes can alter a neural network's object classification while appearing to leave human category judgments stable. That mismatch has been used to question neural networks as models of human vision. This paper examines whether the mismatch depends on which network generates the image perturbation.

Perturbations produced by standard networks do leave human object-category judgments highly stable in the tested small-norm regime. Robustified networks, however, find perturbations within that same regime that strongly disrupt human judgments. The resulting human sensitivity approaches the level observed in the robustified networks, challenging the presumed stability of human perception under these changes.

The authors also demonstrate targeted interventions: robustified networks guide image modifications that shift human category judgments toward specified percepts. The result goes beyond inducing arbitrary errors by showing control over the direction of a perceptual change. These findings support the use of such networks to design strong, precise interventions on human object perception in the studied setting.
neurips-2023-strong-and-precise-modulati.tldr: Robustified neural networks find small image perturbations that strongly and selectively change human object-category judgments.

paragraphs: A generative model can benefit from respecting known conditional independencies among observed variables. This paper introduces Structured Neural Networks, or StrNNs, which encode desired structure by masking pathways through a network. The architecture thereby restricts which inputs can influence particular parts of the modeled function.

The authors connect mask construction to binary matrix factorization and use that relationship to ensure the intended independencies are respected. Designing these masks is an NP-hard problem, so they develop practical algorithms with objectives that control the resulting architecture. This makes structural constraints part of the network design process rather than something the model must discover entirely from data.

Applications include binary and Gaussian density estimation, real-valued density estimation with structured autoregressive and continuous normalizing flows, and interventional and counterfactual analysis using structured autoregressive flows. These demonstrations show how the same architectural principle can support several modeling tasks. The work opens a route toward data-efficient generative modeling and causal effect estimation with structurally constrained flows.
neurips-2023-structured-neural-networks-.tldr: StrNN masks neural-network pathways to enforce desired independencies, supporting structured density estimation and causal analysis with normalizing flows.

paragraphs: Machine learning for molecules, proteins, and crystalline materials depends on how geometric structure is represented. The paper addresses a fragmented landscape of symmetry-informed methods and a knowledge gap between machine learning and scientific communities. Its contribution combines an organizing framework with a platform for comparing methods across scientific tasks.

The authors group existing approaches into three categories: invariant methods, equivariant methods using spherical frame bases, and equivariant methods using vector frame bases. This classification provides a shared vocabulary for understanding different geometric strategies. Their Geom3D platform brings together 16 symmetry-informed representation models and 14 geometric pretraining methods across 52 tasks.

The task collection covers small molecules, proteins, and crystalline materials, allowing researchers to investigate representation choices across several kinds of scientific data. The intended value is a more accessible basis for benchmarking and informed method selection. The abstract presents this broad comparison infrastructure and taxonomy, rather than claiming that one representation strategy is universally best across the covered applications.
neurips-2023-symmetry-informed-geometric.tldr: Geom3D organizes symmetry-informed geometric learning and benchmarks 16 representation models and 14 pretraining methods across 52 scientific tasks.

paragraphs: Auditing private machine learning can involve inserting specially designed examples, called canaries, and testing how their presence affects a trained model. This paper develops a rigorous way to use multiple randomized canaries together, aiming to extract more statistical evidence from each privately trained model.

The first component, Lifted Differential Privacy, extends the privacy definition to randomized datasets. The audit then compares training with K canaries against training with one omitted. Drawing canaries independently from the same distribution creates symmetry that allows each model to support a separate statistical test for every canary.

Those tests can be correlated, so the third component introduces confidence intervals that adapt to empirical higher-order correlations among their statistics. Combining randomized design, model reuse, and correlation-aware uncertainty estimates yields significant theoretical and empirical improvements in sample complexity on synthetic and real data. The framework can also incorporate stronger canary designs, making the statistical procedure compatible with advances in how audit examples are constructed.
neurips-2023-unleashing-the-power-of-ran.tldr: Randomized canaries, reusable model tests, and correlation-aware confidence intervals improve the sample efficiency of differential-privacy audits.

paragraphs: Graph-based approximate nearest-neighbor search is widely useful for large datasets, but strong practical performance does not by itself establish worst-case guarantees. This paper studies both provable efficiency and difficult instances for implementations including HNSW, NSG, and DiskANN.

For DiskANN's slow-preprocessing version, the authors prove a constant approximation ratio with polylogarithmic query time when the dataset has bounded intrinsic dimension. Both the preprocessing variant and the dimension condition are part of the result. The guarantee establishes efficient approximate retrieval within that setting, rather than covering every graph-based implementation.

For the other studied variants, including fast-preprocessing DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG, the authors construct families of instances where empirical query time grows linearly with dataset size to reach reasonable accuracy. One DiskANN example requires at least one tenth of the dataset size in search steps before encountering any of the five nearest neighbors. These findings identify worst-case limits alongside the positive guarantee, showing why implementation choices and data conditions matter.
neurips-2023-worst-case-performance-of-p.tldr: Slow-preprocessing DiskANN has conditional search guarantees, while constructed instances expose linear query costs for other popular graph-based variants.
